entries.title: Daniel 5:1
segments:
Belshazzar; the last king of Babylon, of whom little is known.  He was probably a grandson of Nebuchadnezzar. 
 
vv 1-3. 
 
When carnal security, pride, and contempt of God and his service are united in a community, its destruction is near.

entries.title: Daniel 5:2
segments: Commanded to bring--silver vessels; see note to

entries.title: Daniel 5:4
segments: Jehovah is nigh to all his true worshippers, to hear and save them; but every false confidence deceives and destroys those who put their trust in it, at the very time when they are loudest in its praises.

entries.title: Daniel 5:5
segments: In scenes of revelry and sinful mirth God is ever present as a witness; and he can in a moment change them into anguish and terror.

entries.title: Daniel 5:6
segments: A guilty conscience makes wicked men tremble before every token of God's presence; for they rightly interpret it as being to them a sign of coming wrath.

entries.title: Daniel 5:10
segments: The queen; probably the queen-mother, who had been the wife of Evil-merodach, Nebuchadnezzar's successor.  She was well acquainted with Daniel, while Belshazzar had never concerned himself to learn his history and merits.

entries.title: Daniel 5:13
segments: In seasons of outward security good and wise men are commonly forgotten, with all the services which they have rendered in past times; and too often their aid and counsel are not sought again till it is too late to avert impending ruin.

entries.title: Daniel 5:22
segments: They who know God's judgments upon others for their sins, and yet fail to be admonished by them, are doubly guilty, and will be punished with proportional severity.

entries.title: Daniel 5:23
segments: Hast lifted up thyself against the Lord of heaven; by putting to a profane use the sacred vessels of his temple.

entries.title: Daniel 5:24
segments:
Then; when thou wast thus treating him with contempt. 
 
  The part of the hand; the "fingers of a man's hand,"
. That nothing except these appeared made the vision more mysterious and terrible.

entries.title: Daniel 5:25
segments:
Mene, mene, tekel, upharsin; that is, "numbered, numbered, weighed, and divided." 
 
Presumptuous sinners can expect no message from God, but one of evil tidings.

entries.title: Daniel 5:27
segments:
vv 27-28. 
 
God will soon take from us our earthly stewardship; then we shall be weighed in the balances of his word, and if found wanting, our doom will be like that of Belshazzar--exceedingly terrible.

entries.title: Daniel 5:28
segments: Peres; that is, "divided," or broken into parts.  "Peres," in the original, is the singular, and "upharsin" the plural of the same word, with "and" prefixed, as if the writing had said, "and divided are the parts of thy kingdom."

entries.title: Daniel 5:30
segments:
Slain; by Cyrus king of Persia, who was at the head of the united armies of Media and Persia.  He had turned the waters of the Euphrates out of their course, and entered the city through its channel during a night of feasting and revelry, about 538 before Christ. 
 
In the midst of pomp and splendor and apparent security, men are often on the very brink of destruction.

entries.title: Daniel 5:31
segments: Darius the Median took the kingdom; Darius is supposed to be the "Cyaxares" of profane historians.  He was the uncle of Cyrus and the king of Media.  Upon the death of Darius, Cyrus united the kingdoms of Media and Persia in his own person.
